Schlesinger, M.E., King, M.J., Sole, K.C. and Davenport, W.G. (2011). Extractive Metallurgy of Copper, 5th edition. Elsevier, Oxford/Amsterdam. ISBN 978-0-08-096789-9. Chapter DOIs of the form 10.1016/B978-0-08-096789-9.100NN-N (e.g. Ch.1 10.1016/B978-0-08-096789-9.10001-0; Ch.22 10.1016/B978-0-08-096789-9.10022-8).

Targeted pass of a 453-page book (PDF is a scan-derived copy with blank pages dropped, so PDF page != printed page; locators are PRINTED page numbers). Main file: 28 technology names, 107 (process,technology) examples. Loaded: comminution electricity per t ore for 8 concentrators (Tables 3.1a-c; crusher and SAG/ball circuit, the grinding SEC is the printed sum of stage 1 + stage 2 with formula); smelting-vessel capacity and matte temperature for 6 Outotec flash furnaces, 2 Noranda and 2 Teniente furnaces (Tables 6.1, 7.2, 7.4), Mitsubishi smelting/slag-cleaning/converting (Tables 9.3-9.4), Peirce-Smith converters (Tables 8.1-8.2), Kennecott flash converting (Table 8.5) and Horne Noranda continuous converter (Table 8.6), direct-to-copper flash furnaces (Table 10.3); electric slag-cleaning kWh/t slag (Table 11.2), slag flotation kWh/t slag (Table 11.4); acid plant capacity and export steam (Tables 12.5-12.6); fire refining fuel 2000-3000 MJ/t (p.237); electrorefining 300-400 kWh/t total and plating kWh/t for 6 refineries (Table 14.6, reprinted from Moats et al. 2007); electrowinning ~2000 kWh/t and 4 plants (Table 17.3); Asarco shaft-furnace gas per t (Table 20.3); Chapter 22 study-estimate capex (per annual t Cu) and direct opex, April 2011 USD, plus section shares turned into derived section capex (formula). Flows: oxygen, coal/oil/coke and blast air per t concentrate/charge/copper/slag derived from printed daily or hourly rates (formula), H2SO4 for agitation leach, steam export per t H2SO4. NOT loaded: Isasmelt/Ausmelt tables (no energy rows), flotation tables (no energy), heap/SX tables (no energy), impurity, slag chemistry, refractory data, reagent dosages, scrap chapters (no numbers). Traps: (1) smelting fuel and oxygen are printed per t concentrate or per t charge while smelter archetypes are per t metal: kept in flows with per-unit stated; concentrate %Cu is in the capacity note. (2) p.351 says electrorefining 200-300 kWh/t, p.269 says 300-400 kWh/t total. (3) Noranda Horne oxygen 349 is printed in the "Hydrocarbon consumption, kg/tonne of charge" row. (4) Table 3.1 prints mill power ratings as "kWh" (meaning kW). (5) Kennecott flash converter natural gas per t uses extreme pairing of printed hourly ranges and daily copper range. (6) Flash furnace Saganoseki coal "70" sits in a kg/h row. (7) Chapter 22 smelter opex ~$80/t concentrate = ~$0.3/kg anode Cu (printed). Smelting fuels have no heating value printed.

Global plant data (Chile, Peru, USA, Japan, Germany, Sweden, Indonesia, Korea, Zambia, Poland, Mexico, Brazil, Philippines, India, Australia, Canada: Horne smelter, Nexans Montreal). Chapter 22 costs: South and North America, 2011.
